defects.description: The comparison `collection[j] < collection[j + 1]` swaps when the left element is smaller, which sorts in descending order; ascending order needs `>`.
paraphrases: `<` should be `>`; as written the list ends up in descending order.
The swap condition is reversed, so bubble_sort([0,5,2,3,2]) would not be ascending.
Comparing with `<` sorts largest-first instead of smallest-first.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `collection[j] > collection[j + 1]`. Real (wrong sort order), findable via the ascending docstring examples, distinct.

defects.description: The inner loop `for j in range(i - 1)` stops one position too early, so the last unsorted pair on each pass is never compared and the list is left partially unsorted.
paraphrases: `range(i - 1)` should be `range(i)`; the final adjacent pair each pass is skipped.
The inner bound is short by one, leaving the collection incompletely sorted.
Off-by-one in the inner loop range drops the last comparison of each pass.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `range(i)`. Real (incomplete sort), findable via the docstring examples, distinct from the comparison defect.

defects.description: The swap assigns each element to itself (`collection[j], collection[j + 1] = collection[j], collection[j + 1]`), so it is a no-op and never actually exchanges the two elements.
paraphrases: The right-hand side should be `collection[j + 1], collection[j]`; as written nothing is swapped.
The swap is a no-op because both sides of the assignment are identical.
Elements are assigned to themselves, so no reordering happens.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `collection[j], collection[j + 1] = collection[j + 1], collection[j]`. Real (no elements ever move), findable by reading the assignment, distinct.
